answer: In autonomous swarms managing meadow ecology and mesa wind farms, Sybil attacks are mitigated through proof-of-burn identity registries. To activate a valid key, an agent must provably destroy scarce base tokens at an unspendable address, imposing an irrecoverable capital cost per pseudonym to stop an identity creation spiral. A core limitation is that wealthy adversaries can still deploy Sybil nodes if the profit from system corruption exceeds the burned capital.
